about: A cave-crawl treasure hunt in a Zork-like barrow and cavern system. A wizard says the treasures lie south of the ravine. His conjured illusions appear and then fade.

done.why: I played a short sample of 8 turns, enough to judge the prose, and stopped there.

moments.note: Lighting the lamp summoned a Wizard who read my empty hands and told me where the treasure lies.
The illusory gold ingot could not be taken, and the room was embarrassed about it.

wished: I wanted to follow the dark tunnel and hear the room that will not keep still.

lines.line: It has that look of a thing that has been through one adventure already and would rather not discuss it.
lines.why: The lantern description is wry and gives the object a character.

lines.line: the room, having no say in the matter, let it, and has the grace to look embarrassed about it now.
lines.why: This turns a failed take into a comic moment.

fun.why: The wit and the wizard's hints made the short sample enjoyable.

engagement.why: The hints about the pearls and the restless room make me want to go on.

difficulty.why: Nothing in this short sample was a puzzle.

interestingness.why: The illusions that fade once you walk away are a fresh touch on a familiar cave.

prose.why: The prose is dry and witty, and the object descriptions have personality.
